newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel to resume shuttle on December 10.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel to resume shuttle on December 10.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc/SA said on Tuesday it plans to resume shuttle passenger train services in a week's time and expects Eurostar express trains to start running tomorrow through the fire-damaged Channel tunnel railway.
Earlier the Inter-Governmental Commission (IGC) of French and British government representatives said the tunnel, which was closed after the fire on November 18, could now be reopened.
"We have got the go-ahead," said a spokeswoman. Our own shuttle tourist service will start on Tuesday next week, the 10th of December," she said.
"It is up to Eurostar to start when they want but I believe they are starting tomorrow," she said.
Eurostar later said it would resume 90 percent of its services from Wednesday.
The IGC said that it was now satisfied it was safe to run passenger services through the second tunnel, while the damaged tunnel was still being repaired.

It said the services should be reduced to six trains an hour but Eurotunnel's spokeswoman said normal traffic was around nine trains an hour including freight shuttles, which the IGC has said cannot restart until an investigation is completed into the causes of the fire, which started on such a vehicle.
